chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Indeed, a scorpion bit the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'May Allah curse you, for you do not care whether it is a believer you harm or an infidel.' Then he called for salt, rubbed it on the wound, and it healed.
Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'If people knew what is in the salt, they would not seek any other antidote with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of salt in Shia hadith regarding healing and prophetic tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith illustrates the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) dual response of spiritual authority and practical remedy, where he cursed the scorpion before applying salt, a practice later validated by Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him). The Imam’s remark underscores the profound medicinal value of salt, suggesting its efficacy is so significant that it would be preferred over other antidotes if its true benefits were known. This narrative reinforces the Shia tradition of combining divine blessing (barakah) with tangible, natural cures.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The scorpion bit Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse you, for you (scorpions) don’t care whether it is a believer that you harm or an Infidel’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for the salt, so he<sup>saww</sup> rubbed it down and pressed it’.
Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what was in the salt, they would not seek any other antidote with it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once scorpion bit the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and he (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘May Allah condemn you. You do not distinguish between a believer and unbeliever and do not know whom you can hurt’. He (the Messenger of Allah) then asked for salt and rubbed it on the bitten place and it calmed down.
Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Had people known that which is in salt they would not seek another antidote.’”
